entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Karibʾīl Watār Yahanʾm, sometimes distinguished as Karib'il Watar II, was probably the most important ruler of early Saba. He is sometimes regarded as the founder of the kingdom proper, as he was responsible for changing the ruler's title from mukarrib to malik.

Karib'il Watar I ruled over Saba around 570 BCE, during a period of great cultural and economic transformation in the region. His reign saw the expansion of trade networks and the establishment of new diplomatic relations with neighboring kingdoms. He also oversaw the development of the kingdom's infrastructure, including the construction of roads and public buildings.

The legacy of Karib'il Watar I can be seen in the many archaeological sites and artifacts that have been discovered in Saba, including the impressive stone structures that still stand today. His impact on the region's history has been significant, and his name remains synonymous with the kingdom's golden age.

The discovery of a 3,000-year-old inscription at the ancient Sabaean temple of Marib has provided valuable insights into Karib'il Watar I's life and reign. The inscription describes him as a wise and just ruler who brought peace and prosperity to his people.

One of the most striking aspects of Karib'il Watar I's legacy is the enduring impact of his reforms on the region's social and political structures. His introduction of the title 'malik' as a formal title for the ruler of Saba has been adopted by many other kingdoms in the region.

The influence of Karib'il Watar I can also be seen in the many cultural and artistic achievements of the Sabaean kingdom. The kingdom's distinctive style of architecture, which combines elements of Egyptian, Greek, and Mesopotamian influences, is still admired today for its beauty and sophistication.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Karib'il Watar I was a key figure in the history of early Saba, and his reforms had a lasting impact on the kingdom's social and political structures. His diplomatic efforts helped to secure peace and stability in the region, and his legacy continues to be felt today.
